raw.assessment: The incumbent plausibly combines useful assembly verification with costly selection, insertion and packing, but their separate contributions are unmeasured. Repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, whereas mixed batches contained every extreme delay: a limiting observation against assuming full assembly is inherently too slow. Layout complexity and batch switching remain confounded. Seventeen reinsertion events warrant investigation, but overlapping widths limit a simple width-only explanation. Customer reports suggest component errors without establishing their precise source; three observed short-partition questions suggest an instruction problem. These observations do not establish pilot success or justify changing geometry or connections.

openings.claim: Staging one order-specific set of parts with a count check before insertion may reduce mixed-layout delays and component errors.
openings.delta: Retains full assembly while replacing shared-bin selection during assembly with an explicit, individually checked kit.
openings.prediction: Against the incumbent at matched layout complexity, staging reduces total selection-plus-checking time and wrong-part events; insertion time need not improve.
openings.probe: Use twelve reusable sample organizers, four per compartment count. Both workers alternate methods with counterbalanced order. Time selection, insertion, checking and packing separately, including kit preparation, and record discrepancies before correction. Retain accepted colors and counts; adopt only if cost and delivery gates pass.
assumptions: Staging fits one bench, the delivery schedule and both cost caps.

openings.claim: A diagram specific to the ordered arrangement, explicitly locating the short partition, may improve unaided customer arrangement.
openings.delta: Replaces the three-layout diagram with an exact-order mapping while preserving supplied parts and rearrangeability.
openings.prediction: Short-partition placement errors and help requests decrease even if physical insertion retries persist.
openings.probe: Reuse verified complete sample sets. Assign the ten participants to matched five-person groups using either diagram; observe first attempts, placement errors, insertion retries and unaided completion. Treat results as directional, then verify the 60-unit targets separately.
assumptions: Ambiguous placement contributes to requests for help.
Diagram preparation and printing fit the time and cost constraints.

raw.assessment: Synthetic observations justify tests, not causal conclusions. Pilot targets and all footprint, capacity, rearrangement, cost, configuration, color and deadline constraints remain binding. Neither alternative is established feasible.

openings.claim: Model provider payment per independently verified complete, customer-achievable order. The provider might invent reusable order-specific picking boards that expose missing or wrong partitions before insertion, then batch similar layouts while preserving order identities.
openings.delta: Outcome payment could make preventing selection errors more valuable than faster insertion alone.
openings.prediction: If picking and switching contribute materially, boards reduce selection/checking time and content errors, especially in mixed layouts. Gaming could favor common layouts or exclude board preparation from timing.
openings.probe: Alternate incumbent and board-assisted picking across matched mixed-layout sample orders using existing parts. Independently audit counts, identities and colors; time preparation, selection, insertion, checking and packing separately. Include difficult orders in the denominator and cost boards before adoption.
assumptions: Selection/switching contributes materially; observations do not isolate it.
Boards and scheduling fit the budget and deadline without reducing accepted configurations.

openings.claim: If payment requires unaided achievement of the ordered arrangement, would the provider supply an assembled base with removable partitions presented on an order-specific placement map instead of fully inserting them before packing?
openings.delta: Tests whether customer placement saves workshop insertion time while outcome payment discourages transferring confusing work to customers.
openings.prediction: Partial assembly may save workshop time but lose customer successes if placement or insertion remains difficult. Coaching participants could disguise failure.
openings.probe: Use ten samples and randomly assign five participants per format, balancing layouts. Independently audit contents; record workshop time, unaided ordered arrangement within the same ten-minute observation window, help requests and insertion retries. Verify unchanged assortment capacity and footprint, map cost and delivery feasibility. This small comparison cannot certify pilot thresholds.
assumptions: Partial assembly is acceptable under the stated sales promise.
The map replaces the existing diagram within both cost limits.

openings.claim: Checked order kits may improve selection; verified-outcome payment could induce reusable picking boards and similar-layout batching.
openings.discriminator: Selection/checking/switching gains need not improve insertion.
openings.probe: Counterbalance both workers across twelve layout-matched samples; include preparation and separate stage times; independently audit counts/colors/identities and difficult orders; cost boards.
openings.uncertainty: Complexity/switching confounded; incentive speculative; excluding difficult orders or preparation could game outcomes.

openings.claim: Exact-order diagrams may clarify short-partition placement.
openings.probe: Ten participants, matched five-person diagram groups; verified sets; observe placement, retries, help and unaided completion.
openings.uncertainty: Ambiguity contribution and preparation cost unknown.

openings.claim: Outcome payment might favor assembled bases with removable partitions on placement maps.
openings.discriminator: Workshop savings versus customer placement/insertion failures.
openings.probe: Ten samples, randomized layout-balanced five-person formats; audit contents; measure workshop time, unaided ten-minute completion, help/retries without coaching.
openings.uncertainty: Sales acceptability and map cost unresolved.

lineage.reason: With Z1; boards, batching and incentives preserved.

post_distill.decision: Probe only. Preserve 30x20cm footprint, assortment, removability, accepted counts/colors and deadline; verify 500 initial/0.40 recurring caps. Width overlap limits width-only explanations. Synthetic small samples cannot certify 60-unit targets: 98% complete, median <=8 minutes, 90% unaided.
